HEADLINE: Product Pages Get 24% Of AI Citations, Reddit & YouTube 4% via @sejournal, @gregjarboe

blog.headline: Why Product Pages Command 24% of AI Citations and What That Means for B2B Founders
blog.angle: AI’s growing reliance on product pages creates tension for founders deciding where to invest—owned content or third-party platforms—and demands a new approach to optimize product pages for both humans and AI to secure visibility and trust.

linkedin.headline: Most B2B brands still treat product pages like digital catalogs—meanwhile, AI is treating them like gospel.
linkedin.angle: Product pages now earn nearly a quarter of AI citations, signaling that founders who optimize these pages for AI and buyers can dominate discovery and trust in B2B e-commerce.

facebook.headline: Product pages get 24% of AI citations, while Reddit and YouTube lag at 4% each.
facebook.angle: A recent citation study reveals product pages as the go-to source for AI-driven B2B discovery—are you investing enough in your owned content to stay visible?

instagram.headline: Product Pages: AI’s Trusted Source
instagram.angle: AI’s citation patterns show product pages are the new authority in B2B discovery—founders ignoring this risk fading into the noise.

threads.thread_hook: AI citations put product pages in the spotlight—24% of all references come from them, dwarfing Reddit and YouTube.
threads.angle: This thread breaks down why founders must rethink product page strategy to balance human readability with AI’s criteria, or lose ground in B2B visibility.

stories.story_question: Are your product pages built for AI as much as buyers?
stories.angle: Exploring the tension founders face between investing in owned product content versus chasing third-party platform traffic as AI reshapes discovery.
